guidance.escalation-pattern: If {sign}, reach out to your vet clinic

first-night.title: First night at home
first-night.body: Put the bed near yours. Quiet whimpering is normal. Soft voice, dim lights. In the morning, a short potty break
first-night.escalation: If your puppy is breathing rapidly and can't settle — reach out to your vet clinic

potty-rhythm.title: Potty rhythm
potty-rhythm.body: A small puppy asks to go roughly every 1–2 hours and after eating, sleeping, or playing. Praise calmly the moment they go outside
potty-rhythm.escalation: If there's no urination at all for a full day — call your clinic

biting.title: Mouthing during play
biting.body: Puppies explore the world with their mouth. If teeth touch your hand, say a soft "ow" and pause for 10 seconds. Then offer a toy
biting.escalation: If your puppy repeatedly breaks an adult's skin to the point of pain — talk to a behavior specialist

crate.title: The crate as a quiet spot
crate.body: The crate isn't a punishment — it's a den. Leave treats inside, keep the door open during the day. Sleep in the crate starts with short 10-minute stretches
crate.escalation: If your puppy panics in the crate for more than 15 minutes — stop the training and talk to a specialist
